LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING REPETITION NON-VERBAL COMMUNICATION INTONATION ENGAGEMENT

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.5: Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you ensure imitation is done properly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: IMITATIVE SPEAKING REPETITION NON-VERBAL COMMUNICATION INTONATION ENGAGEMENT
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: IMITATIVE SPEAKING REPETITION NON-VERBAL COMMUNICATION INTONATION ENGAGEMENT
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you ensure imitation is done properly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Imitative Speaking Repetition Non-verbal communication Intonation Engagement means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate mastery of vocabulary and expressions in oral interactions.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
